referencePatternsToCopy.label: Event detail and RSVP flow
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy an event detail layout: title, date/time, location, host, capacity/status chip, attendee context, RSVP action, and confirmation state.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

findings.summary: Camera Club, Member Social Space, Ad-Free Community, and Data Portability repeatedly use the same primary action-card shell with generic chips and templated copy. These surfaces do not yet feel like distinct domain-native product screens for the target communities.
findings.requiredFix: Remediate the visible product UX issue, recapture screenshots, and rerun the LLM vision UX review.

findings.summary: The screenshots for 26 workflow/persona paths do not visibly prove complete lifecycle states. Result screens often end at generic Current state or Saved/Active panels instead of durable receipts, receiver states, continuation paths, or alternate/change/reject actions.
findings.requiredFix: Remediate the visible product UX issue, recapture screenshots, and rerun the LLM vision UX review.

findings.summary: The overall experience cannot pass as a rich production community product while major areas still look like workflow-state cards and while lifecycle closure remains incomplete, even though screenshot hashes are fresh and deterministic visual inspection reports no pixel-level blockers.
findings.requiredFix: Remediate the visible product UX issue, recapture screenshots, and rerun the LLM vision UX review.

findings.title: Workflow lifecycle UX is incomplete
findings.summary: 26 workflow/persona lifecycle scorecards failed. The UI is still proving action-card completion rather than full production workflow lifecycles.
findings.requiredFix: Use the failed lifecycle scorecards to add concrete objects, decision information, semantic primary and alternate actions, persistent result state, and receiver/continuation state before recapturing evidence.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Some communities show readable spacing and hierarchy, but repeated card shells and templated status copy in Camera Club, Member Social Space, Ad-Free Community, and Data Portability keep the UI below a modern shippable product bar.
holisticQuestionAnswers.summary: Repeated surfaces and templated copy remain visible.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does this feel like a rich product experience for the community and persona rather than an implementation workflow surface?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Garden Club, Book Club, HOA, and parts of Masjid Nur show concrete community content, but several personas still see generic task cards rather than full product flows such as a real thread, checkout, ad-off entitlement, gear loan, or export console.
holisticQuestionAnswers.summary: Several major areas still read as generic task cards.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the information architecture centered on real community content and jobs-to-be-done?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: The app often groups screens around domain sections, but whole areas are still organized as repeated workflow/state surfaces with labels like Current state, Status notice, Result visible, Restore path, and Local package details instead of navigable community content and jobs-to-be-done.
holisticQuestionAnswers.summary: Community IA is improved but still partially workflow-state oriented.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are primary surfaces domain-native rather than repeated workflow cards?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Screenshots still show repeated primary card surfaces across unrelated workflows: the same icon, title, summary, status chips, current-state panel, saved/result panel, and bottom support section recur across camera, platform social, ad-off, and export flows.
holisticQuestionAnswers.summary: Repeated product shell remains a major blocker.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Concrete content and actions are visible in many rows, but 26 workflow/persona paths still lack convincing lifecycle closure from pixels: alternate/change/reject affordances, persistent receipt/result, receiver or continuation states, or task-specific decision data are missing or generic.
holisticQuestionAnswers.summary: Lifecycle closure remains incomplete across 26 workflow/persona paths.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Some communities show readable spacing and hierarchy, but repeated card shells and templated status copy in Camera Club, Member Social Space, Ad-Free Community, and Data Portability keep the UI below a modern shippable product bar.
holisticQuestionAnswers.summary: Repeated surfaces and templated copy remain visible.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does this feel like a rich product experience for the community and persona rather than an implementation workflow surface?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Garden Club, Book Club, HOA, and parts of Masjid Nur show concrete community content, but several personas still see generic task cards rather than full product flows such as a real thread, checkout, ad-off entitlement, gear loan, or export console.
holisticQuestionAnswers.summary: Several major areas still read as generic task cards.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the information architecture centered on real community content and jobs-to-be-done?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: The app often groups screens around domain sections, but whole areas are still organized as repeated workflow/state surfaces with labels like Current state, Status notice, Result visible, Restore path, and Local package details instead of navigable community content and jobs-to-be-done.
holisticQuestionAnswers.summary: Community IA is improved but still partially workflow-state oriented.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are primary surfaces domain-native rather than repeated workflow cards?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Screenshots still show repeated primary card surfaces across unrelated workflows: the same icon, title, summary, status chips, current-state panel, saved/result panel, and bottom support section recur across camera, platform social, ad-off, and export flows.
holisticQuestionAnswers.summary: Repeated product shell remains a major blocker.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
holisticQuestionAnswers.why: Concrete content and actions are visible in many rows, but 26 workflow/persona paths still lack convincing lifecycle closure from pixels: alternate/change/reject affordances, persistent receipt/result, receiver or continuation states, or task-specific decision data are missing or generic.
holisticQuestionAnswers.summary: Lifecycle closure remains incomplete across 26 workflow/persona paths.

findings.summary: Camera Club, Member Social Space, Ad-Free Community, and Data Portability repeatedly use the same primary action-card shell with generic chips and templated copy. These surfaces do not yet feel like distinct domain-native product screens for the target communities.
findings.requiredFix: Remediate the visible product UX issue, recapture screenshots, and rerun the LLM vision UX review.

findings.summary: The screenshots for 26 workflow/persona paths do not visibly prove complete lifecycle states. Result screens often end at generic Current state or Saved/Active panels instead of durable receipts, receiver states, continuation paths, or alternate/change/reject actions.
findings.requiredFix: Remediate the visible product UX issue, recapture screenshots, and rerun the LLM vision UX review.

findings.summary: The overall experience cannot pass as a rich production community product while major areas still look like workflow-state cards and while lifecycle closure remains incomplete, even though screenshot hashes are fresh and deterministic visual inspection reports no pixel-level blockers.
findings.requiredFix: Remediate the visible product UX issue, recapture screenshots, and rerun the LLM vision UX review.

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.question: Does the whole experience feel like a real production community app for the target users, not merely an implemented workflow harness?
deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.why: The review cannot claim production-grade UX while workflow/persona lifecycle evidence, direct-question evidence, or screenshot visual inspection is incomplete/failing.
deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.requiredFix: Complete workflow/persona coverage, lifecycle scorecards, and remediate visual/layout failures before claiming production-grade UX.

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.why: 0 rows use non-screen visible text sources, 26 lifecycle scorecards fail, and 0 rows have visual/layout blockers, so the judge cannot make a reliable modern-UI claim.
deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.requiredFix: Use screenshot-derived visible text, fix incomplete workflow lifecycles, and fix detected checklist, repeated-card, thin-content, or weak-identity visual blockers before rerunning the judge.

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.question: Is the overall information architecture organized around community content and real jobs-to-be-done instead of workflow lists or validation surfaces?
deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.why: Failing workflow/persona lifecycle scorecards or visual blockers prevent a holistic community IA pass.
deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.requiredFix: Replace incomplete workflow-card UX with lifecycle-complete domain-native community sections and rerun scorecards.

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.question: Does the visible UI avoid blocking or major overlap, clipping, crowding, default-scaffold, repeated-card, checklist-modal, and thin-content defects?

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.requiredFix: Complete screenshot-backed review rows, fix incomplete workflow lifecycles, and remediate any row-level layout/content defects.
